question: Can a vLLM 4-bit build of Nemotron-3.5-Bolt beat the llama.cpp Bolt profile on two RX 7900 XTX?

candidate.code_check: All Python, tokenizer, chat-template and processor files have the same git blob ids as nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-74B-A9B-BF16 rev 567021037ff88364143e24ea05e6abd0f72086ff; config differs only in quantization_config, dtype and key order.

vllm_settings.moe_backend: TritonWNA16Experts (the gfx1100 RDNA3 MoE kernel accepts only compressed-tensors checkpoints)

vllm-autoround-w4a16-64k.engine: vLLM 0.32.1rc1.dev36+ge68efc685.rocm72, TP2, Triton WNA16 MoE, BF16 KV, 64K

short_prompts.code: Write a Python function that merges two sorted lists. Explain its time and space complexity.
short_prompts.prose: Write a short story about a lighthouse keeper finding a letter.

method.prefill: three fresh ~8192-token marker prompts, 64-output cap (Muse 1024), greedy; salt before content defeats prefix reuse
method.ttft: monotonic request submission to first content or reasoning SSE delta
method.warmup: excluded short warm-up for each workload; models loaded before timing
method.context: production configured windows; no maximum-window claim from these probes

limits: Three timed trials per task; screening, not statistical proof.
Tool calling and constrained JSON were not tested on vLLM (no tool parser configured).
Vision/audio towers were not loaded (--language-model-only); the llama.cpp profile is also text-only.
vLLM prefill uses the engine prefill phase; llama.cpp uses native timings, as in the shared method.
Single uploader quantization; quality beyond marker retrieval and arithmetic was not evaluated.
